reference: GNU coreutils sort invoked by system Bash is the independent oracle. Fixtures are generated with a Bash LCG; GNU tr/tail/cat only post-process them.
coverage: -f and key f fold to upper case
External sort: spilled runs, multi-level merge, keys, -u, -s, -z, -o onto an input, standard input, failure to create a run
Exit status 2 for trouble and 1 for -c disorder
G68: --debug annotations and key warnings (C locale).
exclusions: Address-space limits (ulimit -v) are not set inside the runner; the default budget derived from RLIMIT_AS is checked in the guest qualification instead.

cases.purpose: -f folds lower case to upper case, so '[' and '_' (between 'Z' and 'a') sort after the letters.
A key with its own f flag uses the same upper-case folding as -f.
-S/--buffer-size and -T/--temporary-directory are accepted in their short, glued and long forms on small input.
cases.script:
mkdir t
for o in '-S 1M' -S10% '--buffer-size=2048' '-T t' -Tt '--temporary-directory=t'; do printf '2
1
3
' | sort $o; done

cases.purpose: An invalid SIZE is a usage error with a diagnostic.
cases.script:
rc=0
printf '1\n' | sort -S 12Q || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: A 4 KiB buffer splits the ~300 KB input into about 150 sorted runs in -T, more than the 32-run merge fan-in, so an intermediate merge level runs; output must equal an in-memory sort.
Runs spilled under a 64 KiB buffer merge correctly for a keyed numeric reverse sort with a secondary key.
-u keeps the first record of each equal-key group across runs, and -s keeps input order across runs.
cases.script:
mkdir t
s=7; for ((i=0; i<12000; i++)); do s=$(( (s*1103515245+12345) % 2147483648 )); if ((i%3)); then w=Beta; else w=alpha; fi; printf '%08d k%d %s\n' $((s % 100000000)) $((i%50)) "$w"; done > in
sort -S 64K -T t -k2,2 -u in
sort -S 64K -T t -s -k3,3f in | tail -c 4000

cases.purpose: -o may name the input: the output is opened only after all runs are written.
cases.script:
mkdir t
s=7; for ((i=0; i<6000; i++)); do s=$(( (s*1103515245+12345) % 2147483648 )); if ((i%3)); then w=Beta; else w=alpha; fi; printf '%08d k%d %s\n' $((s % 100000000)) $((i%50)) "$w"; done > in
sort -S 64K -T t -o in in
cat in

cases.purpose: Standard input (a pipe of unknown size) spills too, with NUL-terminated records and a final record lacking its terminator.
cases.script:
mkdir t
s=7; for ((i=0; i<8000; i++)); do s=$(( (s*1103515245+12345) % 2147483648 )); if ((i%3)); then w=Beta; else w=alpha; fi; printf '%08d k%d %s
' $((s % 100000000)) $((i%50)) "$w"; done > in
{ tr '
' '\0' < in; printf 'tail-no-nul'; } | sort -z -S 64K -T t | tr '\0' '
'

cases.purpose: When a run must be written and -T names a missing directory, sort fails with a diagnostic. compare_tree is off because GNU leaves a partial or empty 'out' depending on when it fails; the status and diagnostic are the contract.
cases.script:
rc=0
s=7; for ((i=0; i<8000; i++)); do s=$(( (s*1103515245+12345) % 2147483648 )); if ((i%3)); then w=Beta; else w=alpha; fi; printf '%08d k%d %s\n' $((s % 100000000)) $((i%50)) "$w"; done > in
sort -S 64K -T missing-dir in > out || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: A missing input is fatal in GNU sort: it is reported, nothing is written and the status is 2 (1 is reserved for -c disorder).
cases.script:
printf 'b\na\n' > present
rc=0
sort present missing || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: -c on unsorted input exits 1, not the trouble status 2.
cases.script:
rc=0
printf 'b\na\n' | sort -c || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: G68: --debug writes GNU's warnings to stderr and underlines each key and the last-resort line, for whole-line, field, character, blank-skipping, numeric, general, human, month, version, reversed, unique and stable sorts.
cases.script:
printf 'b 2	a
  a 10	x
c -3.5	y
foo

Jan 5K
 Feb 1.5M
' > in
for o in '' -n -r -u -s -b -k2 -k2n -k2,2n -k2,2 -k1,1 -k1.2,1.3 -k2,2g -k1,1M -M -nr '-k2,2n -r' '-k2,2n -k1,1' '-u -k2,2n' '-s -k1,1 -r' -k3,2 -f '-d -k1,1' -k2b,2 -k1.2b,1.3b -g -h -V -k2,2V '-t. -k1n' '-n -t- -k1,2' '-t: -k2'; do
  printf '== %s
' "$o"
  sort --debug $o in 2>&1
done

cases.purpose: G68: --debug with a tab separator shows tabs as '>' and counts each as one column; with -z the record ends with a newline in the annotated output.
cases.script:
printf 'b 2	a
  a 10	x
c -3.5	y
foo

Jan 5K
 Feb 1.5M
' > in
t=$(printf '	')
sort --debug -t "$t" -k2,2 in 2>&1
sort --debug -t "$t" -k2n in 2>&1
printf 'a 2\0b 1\0' | sort --debug -z -k2,2n 2>&1

cases.purpose: G68: --debug with -c, -C or -o fails with status 2.
cases.script:
printf 'a\n' > in
for o in -c -C '-o out'; do rc=0; sort --debug $o in || rc=$?; echo "$o rc=$rc"; done
[ ! -e out ] && echo no-out

cases.purpose: G73: the -c disorder diagnostic starts "sort: " as GNU sort's does, not with the builtin's internal name, so the /bin shim needs no stderr rewriting.
cases.script:
rc=0
printf 'b\na\n' | sort -c || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"
